blocks.text: Head of the English Language Department
Head of the Theory and Practice of Translation Department
Head of the German Language Department

Dear students, faculty, partners, and guests! The Faculty of European Civilizations is a place where boundaries blur and new meanings are born. We educate those who master the power of words and bridge cultures: specialists in philology, translation, and linguistics. We believe that university years are a time for bold discoveries. Our faculty provides all the necessary conditions for your academic, creative, and personal growth. Our graduates successfully build their careers both in Kyrgyzstan and abroad. Welcome to a community of world-ready leaders! Let’s write your success story together!

The Faculty of European Civilizations (FEC) is a leading department of the university, founded in 1992. Candidate of Philological Sciences, Associate Professor Narynkul Kuseinovna Irsalieva stood at the origins of its formation and development. Over the years of successful work, the FEC has trained more than 10 thousand highly demanded teachers of English and German, linguists, and translators

The mission of the faculty is to train highly qualified specialists in the field of philological education and translation studies with proficiency in foreign languages who meet the national interests of the country and remain competitive in the modern labor market. The main goal of the faculty is to unlock the potential of every student, transforming them into independent, responsible, and sought-after professionals through innovative teaching systems. Student life at the faculty is a dynamic space for professional and personal growth. Future foreign language teachers, linguists, translators, and philologists actively engage in research, present at conferences, and win prestigious international olympiads.

In addition to their studies, students vibrantly express themselves in creative activities, sports, and social projects, developing leadership qualities and teamwork skills. Thanks to rigorous training, our graduates are highly demanded in the market: they build successful careers in major international companies, the media industry, analytical centers, and educational institutions, as well as pursue further education at the world's leading universities.

Founded on September 1, 1992, the Department of English Language has become one of the leading divisions of the Faculty of European Civilizations. It is a hub of academic excellence and innovation, where classical traditions of teaching are harmoniously combined with modern educational technologies. For more than three decades, we have been shaping generations of professionals who master English at the level of international standards and confidently work in education, science, culture, and business.

The primary mission of the Department is to train highly qualified specialists in philology and philological education, capable of thriving in a multilingual and multicultural world. Our graduates do not simply know English — they use it as a powerful tool for professional success, scientific creativity, and intercultural dialogue.

Our goal is not only to teach, but to form educators of a new generation: globally minded professionals with critical literacy and pedagogical expertise, able to build bridges between cultures, inspire students, and transform the future of education.
Developing modern methods of teaching English as a means of professional and cultural communication.
Studying the language in the context of the social, cultural, and political life of its speakers, while comparing it with native language and culture.
Creating a model for training English teachers, intercultural communication experts, and language specialists that meets the demands of the 21st century.
High-quality English language teaching aligned with international standards.
Educational and cultural outreach work with students.

Founded on September 1, 1992, the German Language Department has become one of the leading divisions of the Faculty of European Civilizations at K. Karasaev BSU. Combining a classical academic foundation and modern educational trends, the German Language Department has been producing high-class specialists for over 30 years. We teach the German language according to strict international standards, opening up broad career prospects for students. Our training allows graduates to confidently build their future in science, teaching, intercultural projects, and large businesses.

The mission of the department is the formation of highly qualified personnel in the fields of philological education, linguistics, and translation studies, capable of competing in a multicultural labor market. Our task is to teach graduates to masterfully use the German language as a fundamental tool for professional self-realization, research activity, and building international dialogue.

Our goal is not just to transfer knowledge, but to look after and raise a new generation of educators: globally-minded leaders with critical thinking and impeccable mastery. We form mentors capable of connecting cultures, inspiring students, and transforming the educational system. For our graduates, a deep knowledge of language, literature, and culture becomes a powerful key to international prospects and continuous career growth.
Innovative linguodidactics: Designing and implementing advanced methodologies of teaching the German language as an effective tool for business, scientific, and intercultural interaction.

Linguo-cultural and comparative analysis: Studying the German language in inseparable connection with the social, cultural, and political reality of the native-speaking countries, as well as the comparative study of foreign and native cultural paradigms.

Modernization of educational standards: Forming an advanced model for training educators, linguists, and experts in intercultural dialogue, fully adapted to the challenges and technologies of the XXI century.
High-quality teaching of the German language according to international standards.
Educational and cultural outreach work with students.

The Department of Germanic Philology was founded in 1999 and was renamed the Department of Translation Theory and Practice in 2004. Currently, it operates as a degree-granting department within the Faculty of European Civilizations. Since its inception, the Department has achieved significant success in training highly qualified specialists for both the education system and various governmental and intergovernmental bodies working in the field of international relations.

Mission of the Department is to train highly qualified specialists in linguistics and translation who are capable of effectively solving professional challenges in the context of globalization and evolving international relations.

The purpose of the department is to ensure a high level of theoretical and practical training for students in full compliance with the State Educational Standards of Higher Professional Education (SES HPE).
Training highly qualified, market-demanded personnel, alongside actively conducting scientific research;
Developing and enhancing the educational and methodological activities of the faculty;
Implementing innovative approaches and improving foreign language teaching technologies.
The Department of Translation Theory and Practice offers student training in the following programs:
○ Mode of study: Full-time, standard duration of study — 5 years.
○ Profiles: "Theory and Methods of Teaching Foreign Languages and Cultures (English)" and "Simultaneous Interpretation (English)".
○ Mode of study: Full-time, standard duration of study — 4 years.

The professional team of the Department, which brings together qualified educators and scholars, ensures a high scientific-theoretical, methodological, and organizational level of instruction, while actively engaging in research activities. To maintain current educational standards and exchange advanced expertise, the department faculty members undergo professional development training courses annually.

Qualification Awarded: BachelorProfile: Foreign LanguageDuration of Study: 4 years (full-time)Languages of Instruction: English, German, Italian and French languagesProgram Description: The “Philological Education” program is aimed at training highly qualified teachers and specialists in the field of philology and intercultural communication. Students master theoretical grammar, lexicology, stylistics and the history of the English and German languages, as well as the theory and practice of translation and the literature of the countries of the studied languages. The program develops psychological-pedagogical and research competencies. Graduates are prepared for effective teaching activities in educational institutions, the implementation of modern methodologies, and successful work in an intercultural environment.

Degree awarded: bachelorProfile: 1. Theory and methods of teaching foreign languages and cultures;2. Simultaneous translationDuration of study: 4 years (full-time)Languages of instruction: English, German, Italian, and French

Program Description: The "Linguistics" Bachelor's program trains experts in translation studies, language teaching, and intercultural communication. Students study the phonetics, grammar, and vocabulary of English and German. The training builds skills to overcome cultural stereotypes for successful operation in an international environment. Graduates are prepared to perform written translation and oral interpretation, as well as effectively teach in schools, colleges, and language centers. A practice-oriented approach, which includes internships and practical training, guarantees high demand in the labor market.

Degree awarded: Bachelor Profile: Teaching of Philological Disciplines Duration of study: 4 years (full-time) Languages of instruction: English, German, Italian, and French Program Description: The "Philology" program is aimed at the fundamental training of specialists in linguistics, literary studies, and intercultural communication. Students comprehensively master the theory, structure, and history of English and German languages, textual criticism, as well as masterpieces of world and domestic literature. The training develops skills in critical text analysis, scientific research, and media content creation. Graduates acquire comprehensive competencies for a successful career in general and higher education, publishing, mass media, analytics, and major international companies.

Program: 550300 Philological Education Degree awarded: Master's Profile: Foreign Language Duration of study:5 years (full-time) Languages of instruction: English Program Description: The "Philological Education" master's program offers advanced-level training for future leaders in education and science. Unlike the basic bachelor's degree, the focus here shifts to deep research, managerial, and expert activities. Master's students conduct independent scientific projects in English philology and literary studies, as well as master innovative technologies and methodologies of higher education. Graduates receive a master's degree and possess all the competencies required for teaching in universities, strategic management of educational processes, and a successful research career.

Master's students conduct independent scientific projects in English philology and literary studies, as well as master innovative technologies and methodologies of higher education. Program: 531100 Linguistics Degree awarded: Master's Profile: Theory and Methodology of Teaching Foreign Languages and Cultures Duration of study: 2 years (full-time) Languages of instruction: English

Program Description: The "Linguistics" master's program is aimed at training top-tier experts for research, project, and managerial activities. The training focuses on the deep analysis of language systems, the theory of intercultural communication, and translation strategies, using the English language as a primary model. Master's students master the methodology of linguistic research, modern digital technologies, and the principles of teaching in higher education. Graduates possess advanced competencies to work as heads of linguistic services, leading analysts, and researchers.
